q: 1. A perfectly elastic body is
options: that body which recovers its original shape completely after removal at force
a body of such a material with a lot of extensibility
a body made of rubber only
a body whose cross-sectional dimensions are very small
explain: A perfectly elastic body is one that recovers its original shape and size completely and instantly upon removal of the deforming force, with no permanent deformation.

q: 2. Permanent set is
options: the force which acts permanently on the body
the shape of the member just after completion of construction
ratio of Poisson's ratio to Young's Modulus
explain: Permanent set refers to the residual, irrecoverable deformation that remains in a material after the load causing it beyond the elastic limit has been removed.

q: 3. Stress concentration near the void is ................ as compared to solid portion.
explain: Voids or discontinuities disrupt the flow of stress lines, causing them to 'bunch up' and increase the local stress intensity.

q: 4. In a case of partially elastic body that part of work done by the external forces during deformation is dissipated in the form of heat, which is developed in the body during
explain: In a partially elastic body, the energy lost as heat corresponds to the non-elastic (permanent/plastic) portion of deformation, since elastic deformation energy is fully recoverable.

q: 5. Hoop stress is
explain: In thin-walled cylinders under internal pressure, hoop stress acts along the circumference and is tensile in nature.

q: 6. The Law "Stress is proportional to strain within certain limits" is formatted by
explain: This is Hooke's Law, formulated by Robert Hooke, stating that stress is proportional to strain within the elastic (proportional) limit.

q: 7. As per elastic theory of design the factor of safety is the ratio of
options: unlimited load to load at yield.
explain: In elastic (working stress) design, factor of safety is defined as the ratio of the yield stress to the actual working (allowable) stress used in design.

q: 8. In a composite bar the load distribution among different materials of which it is made is based on the assumption that all the materials will have
explain: In a composite bar, since all constituent materials are rigidly connected and deform together, they undergo the same strain, and load distribution is derived from this compatibility condition.

q: 9. The elongation of conical bar under its own weight is equal to
options: that of prismatic bar of same length
one half that of a prismatic bar of same length
one third that of a prismatic bar of same length
one fourth that of a prismatic bar of same length
explain: Integrating the varying cross-section of a conical bar under self-weight gives an elongation equal to one-third of that of an equivalent prismatic bar of the same length.

q: 10. The load on spring per unit deflection is called
explain: Stiffness is defined as the load required to produce unit deflection in a spring (k = W/δ).

q: 11. The strain energy stored in a spring when subjected to greatest load without being permanently distorted is
explain: Proof resilience is the maximum strain energy a spring can store without undergoing permanent set (i.e., up to the elastic limit).

q: 12. Modulus of the Rigidity is the ratio of
options: poisson's ratio to unlimited strength in compression
explain: Modulus of Rigidity (G), by definition, is the ratio of shear stress to shear strain within the elastic limit.

q: 13. A beam of uniform strength has at every cross section same
explain: A beam of uniform strength is designed such that the maximum bending stress is the same (equal to allowable stress) at every cross-section, even though the moment and dimensions vary.

q: 14. For no torsion, the plane of bending should
options: be parallel to one of the principal axes
pass through shear center of section
pass through neutral axis of the section
pass through cg of the section
explain: To avoid inducing torsion in an unsymmetrical section, the plane of the transverse load (bending) must pass through the shear center of the section.

q: 15. Buckling load for a given column depends upon
options: both length and least lateral dimension
explain: Euler's buckling load formula (P = π²EI/Le²) depends on both the effective length of the column and the moment of inertia (related to the least lateral dimension).

q: 16. A strut is member which
options: is subjected to shear force predominantly
is subjected to axial compressive predominantly
is subjected to bending moment and shear force along with any axial force
explain: A strut is defined as a structural member primarily subjected to axial compressive force.

q: 17. The angle between the two principal planes is
explain: The two principal planes (planes of maximum and minimum normal stress) are always mutually perpendicular, i.e. at 90° to each other.

q: 18. If an element of a specimen of brittle material is subjected to shear stress, the crack propagation if occurs, will be inclined to the sides of the element at
explain: Under pure shear, the maximum tensile (principal) stress acts at 45° to the shear planes, and brittle materials fail along this plane of maximum tensile stress, so cracks propagate at 45° to the sides.

q: 19. Bulk Modulus, Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio are connected by the relation
explain: The standard elastic relation connecting Young's modulus E, bulk modulus K and Poisson's ratio (1/m) is E = 3K(1 − 2/m).

q: 20. In the case of uniaxial tension the angle between the plane carrying maximum shear stress and direction of tensile force will be
explain: For uniaxial tension, the plane of maximum shear stress is inclined at 45° to the direction (axis) of the applied tensile force.

q: 21. The maximum shear stress from a Mohr's circle is given by
options: the distance of centre from the origin
the distance of farthest point on the mohr's circle from origin
explain: On Mohr's circle, the vertical extent (top or bottom point) represents the maximum shear stress, which equals the radius of the circle.

q: 22. An element is subjected to two equal and like stress σ, on two mutually perpendicular planes. The shape of the Mohr's circle will be
explain: When both principal stresses are equal (σ1=σ2=σ), the Mohr's circle degenerates to a single point on the normal-stress axis, since there is no shear stress on any plane.

q: 23. Stress may be defined as
explain: Stress is fundamentally defined as the internal force per unit cross-sectional area.

q: 24. Stress may be expressed in Newton's
explain: In engineering practice (especially for structural/mechanical stresses), stress is conventionally expressed in N/mm² (MPa) due to convenient magnitude.

q: 25. A material is said to be perfectly elastic if
options: it regains its original shape on removal of the load
it regains its original shape partially on removal of the load
it doesn't regain its original shape at all
explain: A perfectly elastic material fully regains its original shape and size immediately upon removal of the applied load.

q: 26. Stress in a beam due to simple bending, is
explain: From the flexure formula σ = My/I, stress varies directly (linearly) proportional to the distance y from the neutral axis.

q: 27. The region of the cross-section of a column in which compressive load may be applied without producing any tensile stress, is known as the core of the cross-section; in circular columns the radius of the core, is
explain: For a circular column of radius r, the core (kernel) has a radius of r/4, within which an eccentric load produces no tensile stress anywhere on the section.

q: 28. In rectangular columns (cross-section b × h), the core is a
options: rectangle of lengths b/2 and h/2
rhombus of diagonals b/3 and h/3
explain: For a rectangular column b×h, the core (middle-third rule region) is a rhombus with diagonals equal to b/3 and h/3.

q: 29. When a rectangular beam is loaded transversely, the maximum compressive force develops on
explain: For a simply supported beam under transverse load, sagging occurs, which puts the top fibers in compression and the bottom fibers in tension.

q: 30. For keeping the stress wholly compressive the load may be applied on a circular column anywhere within a concentric circle of diameter
explain: For a circular column of diameter d, the core (no-tension zone) is a concentric circle of diameter d/4, within which the eccentric load keeps stress wholly compressive.

q: 31. To ascertain the maximum permissible eccentricity of loads on circular columns, the rule generally followed, is
explain: The 'middle third rule' states that a load must be kept within the middle third of the section width/diameter to avoid tension, which is the generally followed rule for columns.

q: 32. The greatest eccentricity which a load W can have without producing tension on the cross-section of a short column of external diameter D and internal diameter d, is
explain: For a hollow circular column, the limiting eccentricity for no tension is derived from the section's core boundary, giving e = (D²+d²)/8D.

q: 33. The deformation of a spring produced by a unit load is called
explain: Flexibility is defined as the deformation produced by a unit load, the reciprocal of stiffness.

q: 34. A composite beam is composed of two equal strips one of brass and other of steel; temperature is raised
explain: Since brass expands more than steel for the same temperature rise, the differential expansion in a bonded strip causes the beam to bend, inducing tension in steel and compression in brass — hence all listed effects occur together.

q: 35. The maximum magnitude of shear stress due to shear force F on a rectangular section area A at the neutral axis is
explain: For a rectangular section, the parabolic shear stress distribution peaks at the neutral axis with a value of 1.5 times the average shear stress (F/A), giving 3F/2A.

q: 36. The ratio of maximum and average shear stresses on a rectangular section is
explain: For a rectangular section, max shear stress = 1.5 × average shear stress (a standard parabolic distribution result), giving a ratio of 1.5.

q: 37. The ratio of maximum and average shear stresses on a circular section is
explain: For a circular section, the ratio of maximum to average shear stress is 4/3, a standard result from integrating the parabolic-type shear distribution over a circle.

q: 38. A bar of square section of area a² is held such that its one of its diameters is vertical; maximum shear stress will develop at a depth h where h is
explain: For a square section oriented with a diagonal vertical, the maximum shear stress occurs at a depth from the top vertex of 3√2·a/4 (with side a), matching option (b).

q: 39. The residual stress in a member is
options: the stress due to the loading on the member
the average of initial and final stresses
instantaneous stress due to sudden loading
explain: Residual stress is the internal stress remaining in a member after all external loads have been removed, arising from non-uniform plastic deformation — best described as a 'deformation stress'.

q: 40. The stress along the contact surface of a rivet and the member is
explain: The stress developed at the contact/bearing surface between two members (e.g., a pin and a plate, or a column base on a footing) is termed bearing stress.

q: 41. In a stressed body the maximum normal stress at any point is always
options: average of maximum and minimum shear stresses
sum of the two normal stresses acting in two principal directions
explain: By definition, a principal stress is the extreme (maximum or minimum) normal stress on any plane through the point with zero shear stress; hence the maximum normal stress is always a principal stress.

q: 42. In a stressed body the minimum normal stress at any point is always
options: average of two normal stresses acting in the two principal directions
difference of two normal stresses in the two principal directions plus shear stresses on those planes
explain: Just as the maximum normal stress is a principal stress, the minimum normal stress at a point is also always a principal stress (the minor principal stress).

q: 43. The maximum shear stress will be equal to
options: on half of the algebraic difference of the maximum and minimum principal stresses at the point
the intensity of shear stress acting on the major principal plane
the shear stress acting on the planes in the direction of two principal directions
explain: Maximum shear stress = (σ1 − σ2)/2, i.e., half the algebraic difference of the two principal stresses.

q: 44. The modulus of elasticity for mild steel is approximately equal to
explain: The Young's modulus (modulus of elasticity) of mild steel is approximately 200-210 kN/mm² (GPa), a standard material property value.

q: 45. Two bars of different materials and same size are subjected to the same tensile force. If the bars have unit elongation in the ratio of 2 : 5, then the ratio of modulus of elasticity of the two materials will be
explain: Since strain (unit elongation) is inversely proportional to E for the same stress (E=stress/strain), a strain ratio of 2:5 gives an E ratio of 5:2.

q: 46. When a bar of length l and diameter d is rigidly fixed at the upper end and hanging freely, then the total elongation produced in the bar due to its own weight is
explain: For a bar hanging under its own weight (w = weight per unit volume), the total elongation is wl²/2E, derived by integrating the varying internal axial force along the length.

q: 47. The length of a conical bar is l, diameter of base is d and weight per unit volume is w. It is fixed at its upper end and hanging freely. The elongation of the bar under the action of its own weight will be
explain: For a conical bar under self-weight, integrating gives an elongation of wl²/6E, consistent with it being one-third of the prismatic bar's wl²/2E value.

q: 48. Strain rosetters are used to
explain: Strain rosettes consist of multiple strain gauges arranged to measure linear (normal) strains in different directions at a point, from which principal strains can be derived.

q: 49. The maximum stress produced in a bar of tapering section is at
explain: For a given axial load, stress = Force/Area, so the smaller cross-sectional area at the smaller end of a tapering bar experiences the maximum stress.

q: 50. Modular ratio of the two materials is the ratio of
explain: Modular ratio, used in composite section analysis, is defined as the ratio of the moduli of elasticity of the two materials involved.
